basic_password.description: Password for basic authentication. Supply it through the secrets directory or `_FILE`.

basic_username.description: Username for basic authentication. Ignored when `bearer_token` is set.

bearer_token.description: Bearer token sent to Alertmanager. Supply it through the secrets directory or `_FILE`.

ca_bundle.description:
PEM bundle of certificate authorities to trust in addition to the system roots.

There is deliberately no option to skip verification. An Alertmanager reachable only over
a certificate nothing trusts is a certificate to fix, not a check to disable.

connect_timeout_secs.description:
Seconds to wait for a connection before trying the next endpoint.

Short on purpose. This is how quickly a dead peer is abandoned for a live one.

endpoints.description:
Base URLs of the Alertmanager peers, tried in order.

List every peer of a high-availability set. Silences gossip between peers, so any of them
accepts a write and the first one that answers is used.

initial_backoff_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait before the first retry.

max_backoff_secs.description: Ceiling on a single wait, in seconds.

max_elapsed_secs.description: Seconds to keep retrying one request before giving up on it.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for a whole request before giving up.

admin.description: Roles that may manage routes and read the effective configuration.

operate.description: Roles that may acknowledge, assign, and add or remove bot-local ignores.

silence.description: Roles that may create, extend and expire Alertmanager silences, which affect every receiver.

view.description: Roles that may read alerts, silences and ignores, and manage their own subscriptions.

capture_reply_text.description:
Whether thread reply text is captured, which needs the privileged `MESSAGE_CONTENT` intent.

A card marks itself responded without this: the author and channel of a reply arrive
without the privileged intent, and that is all the detection needs. Only the text of the
reply is gated, so leaving this off costs nothing except the reply preview.

dev_guild_id.description:
Guild to register slash commands into. Registration is global when unset.

Guild-scoped commands appear immediately; global ones take up to an hour to propagate.
Set this in development and leave it unset in production.

token.description:
Bot token. Supply it through `DAM_DISCORD__TOKEN_FILE` or the secrets directory.

Passing it as a plain environment variable puts it in the output of `docker inspect` and
in any crash reporter that captures the environment.

deadman_window_secs.description:
Seconds without a webhook delivery after which the deadman trips.

It trips only while Alertmanager is unreachable as well.

dedupe_ignore_labels.description:
Labels that do not decide which card an alert is shown on.

Alertmanager's fingerprint covers every label, so a label whose value churns gives one
condition a new fingerprint, and a new card, each time it changes. Naming such a label here
puts every alert that differs only in it onto one card: the card follows whichever of them
is firing and resolves when the last one does. `pod` and `instance` are the usual
candidates on Kubernetes, where a rollout replaces both. Per-alert routes only; a group
route is already keyed by Alertmanager's group.

dispatchers.description:
Outbox dispatcher workers.

Work is hashed into one lane per worker by its dedupe key, so every effect for one alert
lands on one worker. Raising this widens the fan-out across alerts and never splits an
alert across two workers.

outbox_batch_size.description: Outbox rows one worker claims per pass.

outbox_lease_secs.description:
Seconds a claimed outbox row stays claimed before a janitor may reclaim it.

The janitor reclaims at three times this, which is the margin for a worker that is slow
rather than dead.

persist_events.description:
Whether every state transition writes a row to `alert_events`.

Turning this off keeps the current `alerts` row and drops the history. The four reasons
the bot keeps its own alert table all rest on the current row, so nothing else changes.

reconcile_interval_secs.description:
Seconds between reconciler polls of the Alertmanager alert set.

The reconciler is the authoritative path. Anything Alertmanager has that the database does
not is injected as a synthetic event, and anything firing in the database that Alertmanager
has not had for two consecutive polls is treated as resolved. That is what makes the bot
converge after a restart or a partition.

regroup_window_secs.description:
Seconds a resolved card stays re-armable.

An alert that fires again inside the window, measured from when its card resolved, turns
that card back to firing, reopens its thread and counts a flap. Past the window a new card
is posted carrying a link to the previous one, which keeps its history.

audit_days.description:
Days of `audit_log`.

Kept far longer than the rest because it is small and it is the record of what people
decided. Check this horizon against what an incident review needs.

events_days.description: Days of `alert_events` history. This is the expensive table.

resolved_days.description: Days a resolved alert and its notification are kept.

forum_threshold.description:
Threshold for forum routes, which is lower.

Creating a forum post is heavier than sending a message and is rate-limited per channel,
so a forum route reaches trouble sooner than a text one.

threshold.description: Alerts on one route inside the window that trigger digest mode.

window_secs.description: Length of the window, in seconds.

bind.description: Address and port to listen on.

body_limit_bytes.description: Largest accepted request body, in bytes.

max_concurrent_requests.description: Requests handled at once. Further requests queue rather than being rejected.

request_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a request may take before the listener abandons it.

shutdown_drain_secs.description: Seconds to let in-flight requests finish during shutdown.

webhook_path.description: Path Alertmanager posts the version-4 envelope to.

webhook_token.description:
Bearer token every webhook request has to carry.

Compared in constant time. A mismatch is a 401 with no body, so a caller learns that the
token was wrong and nothing about how it was wrong. Leaving this unset disables the check
and is only defensible where the listener is unreachable from outside the namespace.

allowed_hosts.description:
Hosts a rendered button may point at.

An empty list rejects every button, which is the safe reading of "nothing was configured".
The scheme is checked separately and is always `http` or `https`.

buttons.description: The buttons themselves, rendered in order.

label.description: Text on the button. Discord truncates past 80 characters.

url.description:
URL template, rendered with `minijinja`.

The template sees `alert`, `labels`, `annotations`, `links` and `window`.

Every substitution in a URL is percent-encoded. A template that interpolates a value
without a filter is refused when the template is compiled, not when it is rendered, so the
mistake surfaces at boot.

when.description:
Expression that has to be truthy for the button to appear.

Leave it unset for a button that always appears. `annotations.runbook_url` is the common
case: no runbook annotation, no runbook button.

grafana_base.description: Grafana base URL, available to templates as `links.grafana_base`.

prometheus_base.description: Prometheus base URL, available to templates as `links.prometheus_base`.

window_lead_secs.description: Seconds of graph shown before the alert started.

window_trail_secs.description: Seconds of graph shown after the alert ended, or after now while it is firing.

admin_channel_id.description:
Channel the deadman and route-health notices post to.

The deadman fires when no webhook has arrived inside the deadman window *and*
Alertmanager is unreachable. Pair it with a `Watchdog` alert in Prometheus, so that
silence on one side is always noise on the other.

metrics_enabled.description: Whether Prometheus metrics are served at `/metrics` on the ingest listener.

debounce_secs.description:
Seconds to coalesce edits to one card before sending them.

Every edit is also skipped when the newly computed render hash matches the stored one, so
a burst of updates that change nothing visible costs no API calls at all.

description_budget.description:
Characters of annotation text a card may carry before it is truncated.

Discord caps an embed at 6000 characters across every field, and a single alert can carry
a five-thousand-character annotation. The truncation marker links to `/alerts show`, which
has the full text.

key_labels.description:
Labels promoted to their own inline field on the card, in order.

Everything else stays in `/alerts show`. Three or four is the useful number; a card that
lists sixty labels is a card nobody reads during an incident.

show_fingerprint.description: Whether the card footer shows a short fingerprint.

thread_archive_after_minutes.description:
Minutes of inactivity after which an alert thread archives.

Discord accepts only 60, 1440, 4320 and 10080. A firing alert holds 10080 regardless, so
that a week-long incident never archives underneath the people working it.

routes.description:
Routes declared in the file, which cannot be edited or deleted from Discord.

Declaring a route here is what makes a deployment reproducible from its manifests. A route
that disappears from this list is disabled rather than deleted, so the notifications it
created keep their history. `/route add` writes the other kind, which lives only in the
database.

continue_to_next.description:
Whether later routes are still evaluated after this one matches.

This is Alertmanager's own `continue`, spelled out because `continue` is a Rust keyword.

enabled.description:
Whether the route is live.

A route removed from this file is disabled rather than deleted, so the notifications it
created keep their foreign key and stay renderable.

after_secs.description:
Seconds a card may stay firing and unacknowledged before it escalates.

Unset disables escalation on this route, which is the default: a route that escalates
without anybody having asked for it is a second mention nobody expected.

roles.description: Role ids the escalation mentions. Falls back to `mentions.roles` when empty.

users.description:
User ids the escalation mentions. Falls back to `mentions.users` when empty.

Naming a person here rather than a role is what makes an escalation reach somebody who is
not watching the channel it fires in.

group_strategy.description: Whether one card covers one alert or one Alertmanager group.

matchers.description:
Alertmanager matcher expression, such as `severity=critical, namespace=~prod-.*`.

The operators are Alertmanager's: `=`, `!=`, `=~` and `!~`. A regex is fully anchored and
matches the empty string when the label is absent, which is what Alertmanager does. A
pattern longer than 512 bytes is refused, and compiled patterns carry size limits, because
these also arrive from `/route add`.

roles.description: Role ids mentioned on a new firing alert.

users.description: User ids mentioned on a new firing alert.

min_severity.description: Lowest severity this route accepts. Every severity passes when unset.

name.description: Name shown in `/route list` and in a card's footer. Unique within a guild.

id.description: Snowflake of the channel, thread or user.

kind.description:
What sort of channel `id` names.

`/route test` checks the channel's actual type against this before the route is accepted,
because posting a plain message to a forum channel fails at delivery time otherwise.

archive_on_resolve.description: Whether a forum post is archived when its alert resolves.

auto_archive_minutes.description:
Minutes of inactivity before a resolved post or thread archives.

Discord accepts 60, 1440, 4320 and 10080. Unset takes
`render.thread_archive_after_minutes`. A card that is still firing holds 10080 whatever
this says, so that a long incident never archives underneath the people working it.

bump_on_state_change.description:
Whether every state change posts a one-line note in the thread.

Editing a message does not bump a forum's activity sort; only a new message does. Without
this, a state change that only edits the card leaves the post buried where it was. The
note also gives the post the readable timeline that an edited-in-place card deliberately
does not keep.

default_tag.description: Tag applied when nothing else resolves, for a channel with `REQUIRE_TAG` set.

label_tags.description:
Labels whose values become tags, at most three.

With `manage_tags`, a value's tag is created the first time a post carries it; without,
a value is applied only when a tag of that name already exists. Use low-cardinality labels
only. A forum channel holds 20 tags and a post holds 5, and the bot refuses to create a new
tag once the channel reaches 18, so an unbounded label exhausts the budget and later posts
lose their tags.

lock_on_resolve.description:
Whether a forum post is locked when its alert resolves and is archived.

Ignored when `archive_on_resolve` is off: a post left open has to stay editable.
A locked thread needs `MANAGE_THREADS` to reopen, and a flap has to reopen one. Without
that permission the notification is marked orphaned and a fresh card is posted, so leave
this off unless the permission is held.

manage_tags.description:
Whether missing forum tags are created, which needs `MANAGE_CHANNELS`.

The state, severity and default tags are created when the gateway connects, and a label
tag the first time a post carries its value. Created tags are non-moderated, so the bot
can apply them as the thread's owner. Off, or without the permission, the bot applies the
tags that already resolve and reports the gap in `/route test`; a missing tag never fails
a notification.

max_pinned.description:
Most of the bot's posts pinned at once in the channel. Zero turns pinning off.

Discord allows one pinned post per forum, so a value above one has no further effect.

pin_min_severity.description:
Lowest severity that pins an unacknowledged post.

Pinned posts are a free "needs attention" tray at the top of the index. Checked when the
post is created and at each state change, so a severity that rises without one waits for
the next. The pin is dropped on acknowledgement or resolution, and a pin that fails is a
warning that never blocks the notification.

severity_tags.description: Whether each post gets a tag named after the alert's severity.

acked.description: Tag for an alert somebody has taken.

firing.description: Tag for an alert that is firing and unacknowledged.

resolved.description: Tag for an alert that has resolved.

silenced.description: Tag for an alert an Alertmanager silence is suppressing.

thread_kind.description:
Whether that thread is visible to the channel or only to invited members.

A private thread is not anchored to the card, so the card has to carry a link to it and
the bot has to invite the mentioned roles' members. Choose it for routes whose labels are
sensitive, and accept both costs.

thread_when.description: When a text-channel route opens a thread for a card.

title_template.description:
Title template for a forum post, rendered with `minijinja` against the alert.

A forum post title is mandatory and 1 to 100 characters. A template that fails to render,
such as one naming a label the alert does not carry, or that renders to only whitespace,
falls back to the thread name: `[SEVERITY] alertname` and the first non-empty
`render.key_labels` value. The title is set when the post is created.

backend.description: Which backend the bot connects to.

acquire_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for a connection from the pool before failing the operation.

migrate_on_start.description: Whether pending migrations run during startup.

url.description:
Connection URL, which carries the password.

Supply it through `DAM_STORAGE__POSTGRES__URL_FILE` or the secrets directory.

acquire_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for a connection from the pool before failing the operation.

max_connections.description: Size of the read pool. The writer is always one connection.

migrate_on_start.description:
Whether pending migrations run during startup.

Set this false where a separate job owns migrations, which is what a `GitOps` deployment
usually wants: the bot then refuses to start against a schema it does not recognise
instead of migrating underneath a running replica.

path.description: Path to the database file, created on first start if it does not exist.

log_format.description: How each log line is written.

log_level.description:
Filter directives for the log stream, in `RUST_LOG` syntax.

A comma-separated list of `target=level` directives with an optional bare level as the
default, so `warn,dam_engine=debug` raises one crate and leaves the rest alone. A directive
that does not parse stops the process rather than being ignored: a filter that silently
reverted to its default would be discovered while reading logs that should have been there.

A bare word is a target name and not a level, so a misspelt `waarn` is read as a directive
about a crate that does not exist. It parses, it stops nothing, and it filters nothing.
Check that a level change took effect.

attach_stacktrace.description:
Whether captured messages carry a stack trace, as panics always do.

Useful while a fault is being chased and expensive afterwards: it captures and symbolicates
a backtrace on every captured message, including the ones that were only ever going to be
counted.

breadcrumb_level.description:
Level at or above which a log record is kept as a breadcrumb behind the next event.

Breadcrumbs never leave the process on their own. They are attached to the event that
follows them, which is what turns "a dispatch failed" into the sequence that led there.

debug.description:
Whether the Sentry client logs its own activity.

For diagnosing reporting that is not arriving, and nothing else. It is noisy, and it prints
the DSN.

dsn.description:
Project DSN. Reporting is off while this is unset.

It is a credential: anyone holding it can write events into the project. Supply it through
`DAM_SENTRY__DSN_FILE` or the secrets directory rather than as a plain environment
variable.

environment.description:
Deployment this process belongs to, which every event is tagged with.

Set deliberately rather than left at the default. Sentry groups, alerts and retention are
all keyed on it, and a staging replica reporting as `production` is worse than one that
reports nothing.

event_level.description: Level at or above which a log record is sent as an event of its own.

max_breadcrumbs.description: How many breadcrumbs are kept behind an event.

release.description:
Release every event is attributed to. Defaults to the bot's own version.

Override it only where the image carries a version this binary does not know, such as a
build that appends a commit to the tag.

sample_rate.description:
Fraction of events that are sent, from `0.0` to `1.0`.

A blunt instrument: it drops whole events at random, so an error that fires once is the one
most likely to be lost. Leave it at `1.0` and shed volume with `event_level` instead.

send_default_pii.description:
Whether events carry the addresses, headers and user identifiers Sentry calls default PII.

Off, and worth leaving off. The alerts this bot handles carry infrastructure labels, and
the Discord side carries user identifiers; neither needs to reach a third party for an
error report to be actionable.

server_name.description:
Host name reported with each event. Defaults to the machine's own.

Worth setting where the machine name is an ephemeral pod hash, which groups nothing.

shutdown_timeout_secs.description:
Seconds to spend delivering whatever is still queued during shutdown.

Spent on the way out, after the listener has stopped, so it lengthens a restart by at most
this much. Zero abandons the queue, which loses exactly the report explaining why the
process is stopping.

span_level.description:
Level at or above which a span joins the trace.

Only this bot's own spans are traced, whatever this says, and there is no key to widen
that. A dependency instruments its internals for its own logs, and the fields it attaches
are debug renderings of whatever the call was holding. None of that belongs with a third
party, and there is enough of it to bury the trace it surrounds.

traces_sample_rate.description:
Fraction of traces that are sent, from `0.0` to `1.0`. Tracing is off at `0.0`.

Every webhook batch, every outbox item, every periodic pass and every slash command is one
trace, so the rate multiplies the busiest path in the process rather than the rarest. Start
low.

Whether captured messages carry a stack trace, as panics always do.

Useful while a fault is being chased and expensive afterwards: it captures and symbolicates
a backtrace on every captured message, including the ones that were only ever going to be
counted.

Whether events carry the addresses, headers and user identifiers Sentry calls default PII.

Off, and worth leaving off. The alerts this bot handles carry infrastructure labels, and
the Discord side carries user identifiers; neither needs to reach a third party for an
error report to be actionable.
How many breadcrumbs are kept behind an event.

Seconds to spend delivering whatever is still queued during shutdown.

Spent on the way out, after the listener has stopped, so it lengthens a restart by at most
this much. Zero abandons the queue, which loses exactly the report explaining why the
process is stopping.

Whether the Sentry client logs its own activity.

For diagnosing reporting that is not arriving, and nothing else. It is noisy, and it prints
the DSN.

continue_to_next.description:
Whether later routes are still evaluated after this one matches.

This is Alertmanager's own `continue`, spelled out because `continue` is a Rust keyword.

enabled.description:
Whether the route is live.

A route removed from this file is disabled rather than deleted, so the notifications it
created keep their foreign key and stay renderable.

after_secs.description:
Seconds a card may stay firing and unacknowledged before it escalates.

Unset disables escalation on this route, which is the default: a route that escalates
without anybody having asked for it is a second mention nobody expected.

roles.description: Role ids the escalation mentions. Falls back to `mentions.roles` when empty.

users.description:
User ids the escalation mentions. Falls back to `mentions.users` when empty.

Naming a person here rather than a role is what makes an escalation reach somebody who is
not watching the channel it fires in.

group_strategy.description: Whether one card covers one alert or one Alertmanager group.

matchers.description:
Alertmanager matcher expression, such as `severity=critical, namespace=~prod-.*`.

The operators are Alertmanager's: `=`, `!=`, `=~` and `!~`. A regex is fully anchored and
matches the empty string when the label is absent, which is what Alertmanager does. A
pattern longer than 512 bytes is refused, and compiled patterns carry size limits, because
these also arrive from `/route add`.

roles.description: Role ids mentioned on a new firing alert.

users.description: User ids mentioned on a new firing alert.

min_severity.description: Lowest severity this route accepts. Every severity passes when unset.

name.description: Name shown in `/route list` and in a card's footer. Unique within a guild.

id.description: Snowflake of the channel, thread or user.

kind.description:
What sort of channel `id` names.

`/route test` checks the channel's actual type against this before the route is accepted,
because posting a plain message to a forum channel fails at delivery time otherwise.

archive_on_resolve.description: Whether a forum post is archived when its alert resolves.

auto_archive_minutes.description:
Minutes of inactivity before a resolved post or thread archives.

Discord accepts 60, 1440, 4320 and 10080. Unset takes
`render.thread_archive_after_minutes`. A card that is still firing holds 10080 whatever
this says, so that a long incident never archives underneath the people working it.

bump_on_state_change.description:
Whether every state change posts a one-line note in the thread.

Editing a message does not bump a forum's activity sort; only a new message does. Without
this, a state change that only edits the card leaves the post buried where it was. The
note also gives the post the readable timeline that an edited-in-place card deliberately
does not keep.

default_tag.description: Tag applied when nothing else resolves, for a channel with `REQUIRE_TAG` set.

label_tags.description:
Labels whose values become tags, at most three.

With `manage_tags`, a value's tag is created the first time a post carries it; without,
a value is applied only when a tag of that name already exists. Use low-cardinality labels
only. A forum channel holds 20 tags and a post holds 5, and the bot refuses to create a new
tag once the channel reaches 18, so an unbounded label exhausts the budget and later posts
lose their tags.

lock_on_resolve.description:
Whether a forum post is locked when its alert resolves and is archived.

Ignored when `archive_on_resolve` is off: a post left open has to stay editable.
A locked thread needs `MANAGE_THREADS` to reopen, and a flap has to reopen one. Without
that permission the notification is marked orphaned and a fresh card is posted, so leave
this off unless the permission is held.

manage_tags.description:
Whether missing forum tags are created, which needs `MANAGE_CHANNELS`.

The state, severity and default tags are created when the gateway connects, and a label
tag the first time a post carries its value. Created tags are non-moderated, so the bot
can apply them as the thread's owner. Off, or without the permission, the bot applies the
tags that already resolve and reports the gap in `/route test`; a missing tag never fails
a notification.

max_pinned.description:
Most of the bot's posts pinned at once in the channel. Zero turns pinning off.

Discord allows one pinned post per forum, so a value above one has no further effect.

pin_min_severity.description:
Lowest severity that pins an unacknowledged post.

Pinned posts are a free "needs attention" tray at the top of the index. Checked when the
post is created and at each state change, so a severity that rises without one waits for
the next. The pin is dropped on acknowledgement or resolution, and a pin that fails is a
warning that never blocks the notification.

severity_tags.description: Whether each post gets a tag named after the alert's severity.

acked.description: Tag for an alert somebody has taken.

firing.description: Tag for an alert that is firing and unacknowledged.

resolved.description: Tag for an alert that has resolved.

silenced.description: Tag for an alert an Alertmanager silence is suppressing.

thread_kind.description:
Whether that thread is visible to the channel or only to invited members.

A private thread is not anchored to the card, so the card has to carry a link to it and
the bot has to invite the mentioned roles' members. Choose it for routes whose labels are
sensitive, and accept both costs.

thread_when.description: When a text-channel route opens a thread for a card.

title_template.description:
Title template for a forum post, rendered with `minijinja` against the alert.

A forum post title is mandatory and 1 to 100 characters. A template that fails to render,
such as one naming a label the alert does not carry, or that renders to only whitespace,
falls back to the thread name: `[SEVERITY] alertname` and the first non-empty
`render.key_labels` value. The title is set when the post is created.

keys.docs:
Routes declared in the file, which cannot be edited or deleted from Discord.

Declaring a route here is what makes a deployment reproducible from its manifests. A route
that disappears from this list is disabled rather than deleted, so the notifications it
created keep their history. `/route add` writes the other kind, which lives only in the
database.

loader.docs: Names the TOML layer: a file, or a directory whose `*.toml` files are all merged in name order.
Names a directory of key-named files — a mounted Kubernetes `Secret` volume. Each file supplies the key its name spells.
